1/ Autonomous fixes from customer support tickets

@Mintlify built an internal system that ingests every customer support ticket, identifies if it's about an issue, and if so, assigns it to a coding agent to fix.

2/ Design prototyping

Designers set up Lovable and Replit with the design system so that engineers can prototype new features quickly.

When building a new feature, an engineer drops the Slack thread where the feature is discussed into Replit or Lovable for a quick prototype

3/ A knowledge retrieval agent

They built a knowledge base agent with access to Notion + Google Drive + meeting notes + Slack + emails + codebase.

When you have any question, on any topic, you just at mention the KB agent in Slack.

It's a simple idea, but makes a difference in

4/ The CEO's personal agent

@handotdev built a Han agent – inspired by personal agents like OpenClaw

This is an agent that has access to all the tools he uses, and is available right in Slack

So instead of switching contexts to read/write to any app, he just asks the Han agent

5/ Email agent

This one helps the team spend less time in emails while still being highly responsive.

It checks emails every morning and marks spam or unimportant messages as read.

It auto-forwards any emails that need to be routed to another team member automatically.

6/ Morning sales brief

Every morning this agent sends a rundown of all customer conversations and in-process deals.

How it's built: @claudeai Cowork cron job using MCPs from @salesforce, @meetgranola, and @tryattention to pull customer conversations and pushes to Slack

7/ The weekly intel agent

Each week it compiles what customers, partners, and adjacent companies shipped, then drops the roundup in a channel.

How it's built: a vibe-coded script on a cron job, calling the @claudeai API with deep-research tools attached.
